articles.title: Bitcoin Fell on 11 of 14 Nasdaq Down Days as Tech Rout Deepens
articles.excerpt: Bitcoin's 30-day correlation with the Nasdaq 100 stood at 0.59 before Thursday, up from 0.13 in early September, per Yahoo Finance price data.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin fell on 11 of the 14 days the Nasdaq 100 closed lower in the 30 trading sessions through Wednesday, a Black Mint count of [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5ENDX/history/) daily closes shows. Thursday followed the pattern.

By 12:53 p.m. ET the Nasdaq 100 was down 5.6%, per [Nasdaq.com](https://www.nasdaq.com/market-activity/index/ndx) and Yahoo Finance quotes, and the S&P 500 was off 3.8%. [AP](https://apnews.com/article/stocks-markets-ai-midterm-oil-trump-7ee9c212805aa5e70cf34d25aab7a36e) said the S&P 500 was on track for its worst drop since April 2025. Bitcoin was down 5.6% over 24 hours near $75,900, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin). Black Mint covered the [first leg of the slide](https://blackmint.markets/news/bitcoin-falls-chip-stock-selloff/) earlier Thursday.

The S&P 500 sat about 5% below its Oct. 6 record close, while the Nasdaq Composite was about 11% below its own, past the 10% line Wall Street calls a correction.

**What a 0.59 reading means**

The score runs from -1 to 1. At 1, two assets move the same direction every day; at 0, one tells you nothing about the other. It measures direction, not size (bitcoin can fall twice as far and still score high), and it says nothing about which market leads.

Over those 30 sessions, bitcoin's daily returns scored 0.59 against the Nasdaq 100 and 0.61 against the S&P 500. Over 90 sessions, both readings were about 0.40. CoinGecko prices give 0.53 for the Nasdaq 100. The 30-day score was 0.13 on Sept. 9 and peaked at 0.69 on Oct. 8.

For scale, an [IMF study](https://www.imf.org/en/blogs/articles/2022/01/11/crypto-prices-move-more-in-sync-with-stocks-posing-new-risks) put the bitcoin-S&P 500 figure at 0.01 for 2017-19 and 0.36 for 2020-21. The IMF tied the jump to investor risk appetite and found spillovers grow in volatile stretches.

**Chipmakers led Thursday while bonds rallied**

The 10-year Treasury yield fell six basis points to 4.83%, a [Bloomberg wrap](https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/nasdaq-100-sinks-5%25-as-chipmaker-selloff-deepens%3a-markets-wrap/92330151) showed, as chip stocks slid on speculation that the new Democratic Congress will tighten rules on AI. Investors "are de-risking until clarity returns," Michael O'Rourke of JonesTrading said there.

Bitcoin miners that rent power to AI firms fell further. IREN was down 16.5% and Cipher Mining 15.1%, Nasdaq.com quotes showed.

*In our opinion: a 0.59 score means bitcoin is trading as part of the tech book right now, tighter than in the 2020-21 stretch the IMF studied. That cuts both ways for holders: it fell with chips Thursday, and it rose with the Nasdaq 100 on Wednesday. The test is the next chip rebound. If bitcoin sits that one out, the link is loosening.*

articles.title: Bitcoin Gives Back Its Election Gains as Nasdaq 100 Drops 5%
articles.excerpt: Ether fell harder, down 7.1% to about $2,266. Bitcoin's CoinGecko price is now its lowest daily reading since Sept. 18, a day after $80,000.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin fell 5.2% over 24 hours to about $76,450 at 11:55 a.m. ET Thursday, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin), as a selloff in chip stocks pulled the Nasdaq 100 down 5.2% by late morning.

That erases Wednesday's bounce. Black Mint reported Wednesday that bitcoin had climbed back above $80,000, and [Investopedia](https://www.investopedia.com/stock-market-today-dow-jones-s-and-p-500-nasdaq-11052026-12237014) put the day's high above $81,000. Thursday's price is the lowest daily reading in CoinGecko's data since Sept. 18.

**Chipmakers led the slide**

A gauge of chip giants fell 10% and Nvidia slid 8%, a [Bloomberg markets wrap](https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/nasdaq-100-sinks-5%25-as-chipmaker-selloff-deepens%3a-markets-wrap/92330151) showed at 11:11 a.m. ET. The S&P 500 was down 3.1%. Bloomberg tied the selling to speculation that congressional Democrats, who won Tuesday's midterms, will tighten rules on the artificial-intelligence industry.

Chris Murphy of Susquehanna International Group said in the same wrap that investors are worried about the pace and funding of AI spending now that more regulation is on the table. Not everyone agreed. Bob Edwards of Edwards Asset Management said he was "not concerned" about what the election means for AI, since "the president still has the veto pen."

Ether dropped further. It was down 7.1% at about $2,266, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/ethereum).

**How a sell-off feeds itself**

Many crypto traders borrow to bet on price moves. When the price runs against a borrowed bet and the trader's collateral (the deposit backing the loan) runs short, the exchange closes the position automatically. Those forced sales add to the selling and can push the price lower still. On Wednesday the same machinery ran in reverse, squeezing traders who had bet on a fall.

Bonds caught a bid as stocks fell. The 10-year Treasury yield slipped five basis points to 4.84%, Bloomberg's data showed.

*In our opinion: two days, two stories. Wednesday's bounce came largely from short bets being forced shut, and Thursday's drop came as bitcoin traded alongside chip stocks rather than apart from them. The number worth watching is $80,000; until bitcoin gets back above it, the election rally is undone on paper.*

articles.title: Bank of England Raises Rates to 4% as Inflation Heads Toward 5%
articles.excerpt: The vote was 8-1, and the lone dissenter wanted a half-point move. The BoE sees UK inflation near 5% by mid-2027 as energy costs climb.
articles.body_md:
The Bank of England raised its key interest rate by 0.25 percentage point to 4% on Thursday, saying higher energy prices tied to the Middle East conflict will push UK inflation to about 5% by the middle of next year.

The [Monetary Policy Committee voted 8-1](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/monetary-policy-summary-and-minutes/2026/november-2026). Catherine Mann wanted a bigger half-point increase, to 4.25%. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/05/interest-rates-inflation-uk.html) noted it is the bank's first hike since August 2023, and that markets had priced in more than a 99% chance of the move, per LSEG data.

**Energy is doing the damage**

UK consumer prices rose 3.5% in the year to September, the minutes say, and the bank's staff expect about 4.5% in early 2027. Brent crude futures averaged $108 a barrel over the 15 UK working days to Oct. 27, 38% above the level in the bank's July report.

Here's the mechanism. Bank Rate is what the BoE pays banks on money they park with it, so it sets the floor for UK borrowing costs. Raising it makes mortgages and business loans dearer, which is meant to cool spending before high fuel bills spread into wages and other prices. Two-year mortgage rates were already up nearly 50 basis points since early September, the minutes show.

**Not all nine see more hikes**

"In view of the news, the case is clear for a 25-basis point rise now," Governor Andrew Bailey said in the minutes. Alan Taylor voted for the hike but framed it narrowly: "this is not the start of a hiking cycle," he said, calling it a "one-for-now" insurance hike.

The 10-year gilt yield was about 5.15%, up 2 basis points, CNBC reported. Bitcoin was down 5.2% over 24 hours at about $76,450 at 11:55 a.m. ET, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin), on a day U.S. chip stocks led a wider selloff.

*In our opinion: the split inside the committee is the real story. One member wanted 50 basis points while another called this a single insurance move. Savers win a little and mortgage holders pay more. The next test lands Dec. 17, when the BoE decides again.*

articles.title: Samsung Wallet Adds USDC Accounts for 82 Million U.S. Galaxy Devices
articles.excerpt: Coinbase holds the coins, Bastion runs the accounts, and New York residents can't sign up. Balances aren't FDIC or SIPC insured, Samsung says.
articles.body_md:
Samsung switched on stablecoin accounts in Samsung Wallet on Thursday, letting eligible U.S. Galaxy users buy, hold and send Circle's USDC, a feature that works on about 82 million compatible devices.

The launch came about a week after the window Samsung set in its [Oct. 7 announcement](https://www.samsungmobilepress.com/articles/samsung-wallet-stablecoin-galaxy-us), which promised the last week of October. [The Block](https://www.theblock.co/news/business/2026-11-05-samsung-wallet-launches-usdc-accounts-solana-us-galaxy-users-434523) and [Decrypt](https://decrypt.co/382586/stablecoins-samsung-wallet-adds-usdc-solana) both reported it live Thursday, running on the Solana blockchain.

**How it works**

USDC is a stablecoin: a token meant to stay worth $1, backed by reserves that issuer Circle manages. In Samsung's version, dollars a user adds from a bank account or card are converted into USDC, and withdrawals turn them back into dollars, Samsung's [support FAQ](https://www.samsung.com/us/support/answer/ANS10013605/) says. Users can send USDC to other Samsung Wallet users, to outside crypto wallets, or to bank accounts in more than 60 countries, where recipients get local currency.

No separate crypto app is needed. Every account access and transfer needs a fingerprint.

**Who handles the money**

Samsung runs the app. Bastion, a licensed money transmitter, runs the custodial wallet and transfers, and the USDC sits in Coinbase's institutional custody. Stripe and its partners, including Bridge, process purchases, and Coinflow handles withdrawals, the FAQ says. There's no fee to open an account. Other fees vary by method and country.

Users can opt into rewards on their balance, capped at 1,500 USDC a year. The FAQ is blunt on risk: balances aren't covered by FDIC, NCUA or SIPC, and transfers can't be reversed. New York residents are excluded.

"We're bringing USDC transfers into Samsung Wallet so eligible Galaxy users can get started without installing another app or managing private keys themselves," Woncheol Chai, who heads Samsung's digital wallet team, said in October.

*In our opinion: running a week behind schedule is forgivable when the product is this simple to reach. The figure to chase is sign-ups, and Samsung hasn't released any yet. Eighty-two million phones can see the button. Its October release also floated in-store stablecoin payments; that's the next step worth watching.*

articles.title: Zcash Upgrade Set to Freeze About $16M Left in Sprout Pool
articles.excerpt: About 12,226 ZEC still sits in the 2016 Sprout pool. NU7 at block 3,543,405 turns off the only transaction format that can spend it.
articles.body_md:
Zcash's NU7 network upgrade is set to make remaining balances in Sprout, the network's original 2016 privacy pool, unspendable once block 3,543,405 arrives, under [ZIP 2003](https://zips.z.cash/zip-2003).

About 12,226 ZEC was still in Sprout as of Thursday morning, [ZecStats](https://zecstats.org/shielded) shows. At about $1,319 per ZEC near 5:57 a.m. ET Thursday, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/zcash), that is roughly $16 million. The coins are not burned and stay in issued supply; owners who keep their keys simply lose a consensus path to move them after activation.

**How the freeze works**

Sprout transfers require version-4 transactions. ZIP 2003 changes the consensus rules so that from NU7 onward the transaction version must be 5 or 6, not 4. Newer pools (Sapling, Orchard and Ironwood) use later formats and are not frozen by this change. ZecStats labels Sprout "Closing: frozen at NU7" and notes the pool has been exit-only for years.

A Zcash Foundation engineering update posted on the [community forum](https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/zf-engineering-update-october-20-november-2-2026/58823) said Zebra 7.0.0 supports NU7 on mainnet at height 3,543,405, planned for around Nov. 5. Exact wall-clock timing depends on how fast miners find blocks. CoinDesk and Crypto Briefing put activation in the Thursday evening to Friday early-Asia window if the chain keeps its prior 75-second target; NU7 also shortens the target block time to 25 seconds after activation, those outlets reported from the upgrade specs.

ZIP 2003 leaves open a future upgrade that could restore spending, and warns that spending may never be re-enabled. Holders who still have Sprout funds need to move them with software that still supports version-4 spends before the activation height. Sprout addresses begin with "zc," which can help people scanning old wallet records.

The public pool balance cannot show who owns the remaining coins or how many keys are lost. Roughly 10,000 ZEC left Sprout over the past week, with most of that move on Sunday, CoinDesk reported from ZecStats history; only a thin amount followed on Wednesday.

*In our opinion: the practical check for readers is whether any old "zc" balance still shows in a wallet before block 3,543,405. The $16 million figure will fall with every successful exit, and ZIP 2003 calls later recovery only a possibility. After activation, the story shifts from a deadline to whether the community ever schedules a recovery path.*

articles.title: France Shelves Stablecoin Tax After Assembly Rejects Budget
articles.excerpt: Lawmakers voted 458–0 against the 2027 revenue section. The Senate gets the government's original text; debate is due to start Nov. 20.
articles.body_md:
France's National Assembly rejected the revenue section of the 2027 finance bill on Nov. 4 by 458 votes to 0, with 2 abstentions, the [official Assembly voting record](https://www.assemblee-nationale.fr/dyn/17/scrutins/9759) shows.

The rejection wipes Assembly-added amendments from the text that now goes to the Senate, including a measure that would have taxed gains when crypto is converted into MiCA-compliant stablecoins, [Journal du Coin](https://journalducoin.com/actualites/budget-2027-rejet-458-voix-taxe-stablecoins/) reported. [The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/news/regulation/france-s-budget-rejection-shelves-stablecoin-tax-and-wallet-reporting) said the crypto measures could return through Senate amendments, with budget debate there scheduled to begin Nov. 20.

**What the stablecoin amendment would have done**

Amendment I-3898, sponsored by lawmaker Nicolas Sansu, would have ended the tax deferral on exchanges of crypto for MiCA-compliant stablecoins, Journal du Coin reported. Under that text, converting bitcoin into a euro- or dollar-tied stablecoin such as USDC would have become a taxable event from Jan. 1, 2027, at France's flat tax rate of 31.4%. The amendment passed the Assembly on Oct. 16 by 38 votes to 37 and lasted 19 days before the revenue section fell.

How French budget procedure works after a first-reading rejection: the government sends the Senate its original bill, not the amended Assembly version. Senators can reintroduce taxes by amendment. Journal du Coin said five crypto-related amendments adopted in the finance committee also drop with the revenue section. Nothing stops the Senate from writing them back in, or a later joint committee from reviving them.

The Assembly vote was unanimous against among those who cast a yes or no. The [Assembly's own news note](https://www.assemblee-nationale.fr/dyn/actualites-accueil-hub/rejet-en-premiere-lecture-du-projet-de-loi-de-finances-pour-2027) confirms the first-reading rejection of the finance bill's first part. For U.S. readers, the practical stake is whether euro-area holders keep the current deferral when they move into regulated stablecoins, and whether similar wallet-reporting ideas return in the upper house.

*In our opinion: the clock to watch is Nov. 20, when the Senate opens the finance debate. The stablecoin conversion tax lived for 19 days on a one-vote margin, then died with a 458–0 revenue rejection. If the Senate majority declines to revive it, the next forks are a joint committee or a fresh Assembly reading, and the Sansu text is not guaranteed a return.*

articles.title: Arkansas Sues Kalshi, Alleging Illegal Gambling Platform
articles.excerpt: Attorney General Tim Griffin filed in Independence County under the Deceptive Trade Practices Act, seeking restitution, penalties and an injunction.
articles.body_md:
Arkansas Attorney General Tim Griffin sued KalshiEX LLC and Kalshi Inc. on Nov. 4, alleging the prediction-market operator offered illegal gambling to Arkansas residents, the [attorney general's office](https://arkansasag.gov/news-release/attorney-general-griffin-sues-prediction-market-kalshi-for-providing-illegal-gambling-platform-in-arkansas/) said.

The civil case was filed in Independence County Circuit Court. Griffin's release says the state seeks restitution, civil penalties, unpaid taxes and injunctive relief under the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act. The [Northwest Arkansas Democrat-Gazette](https://www.nwaonline.com/news/2026/nov/04/arkansas-attorney-general-sues-kalshi-vgw/) and the [Arkansas Advocate](https://arkansasadvocate.com/2026/11/04/arkansas-accuses-prediction-market-online-gaming-platform-of-operating-illegal-gambling/) reported the same filing date and court.

**What the state alleges**

Griffin's statement says Kalshi lets users wager on election and sports outcomes, among other events without Arkansas gambling licenses, taxes or age limits that apply to licensed operators. The release says the platform is open to people as young as 18, while Arkansas sets a 21-and-over floor for regulated casino and sports wagering. It points to Kalshi's self-exclusion tools and deposit limits, plus problem-gambling resources as evidence the company treats the product like gambling even while calling it a prediction market.

"Arkansas law is concerned with substance, not semantics," Griffin said in the release. That quote is the state's framing. The complaint, as summarized by the Democrat-Gazette and Arkansas Advocate, asks the court to declare Deceptive Trade Practices Act violations and order refunds for in-state users who lost money.

We found no public statement from Kalshi responding to the Arkansas complaint as of 6:10 a.m. ET Thursday. The company has previously described its contracts as event contracts overseen by the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission. That federal framing is the core dispute in several state cases.

Prediction markets let users buy and sell contracts that pay out based on whether an event happens. Kalshi is registered with the CFTC as a designated contract market. States that sue argue sports and entertainment contracts are still illegal wagers under local law even if a federal futures regulator lists them.

Griffin filed a separate suit the same day against VGW, the operator behind Chumba Casino and related sweepstakes games, the Democrat-Gazette reported. Arkansas joins other states that have targeted Kalshi in court.

*In our opinion: the forum fight is the stake. If state consumer-protection suits can reclassify CFTC-listed event contracts as illegal gambling, the product map for sports and election markets shrinks state by state. Watch for Kalshi's first filing in Independence County and whether other attorneys general copy Arkansas's Deceptive Trade Practices Act path.*

articles.title: XRP Ledger Closes Burn Bug That Let Delegates Mint Tokens
articles.excerpt: fixCleanup3_4_0 went live Nov. 4 at 2:52 p.m. UTC. Native XRP supply was never at risk; the flaw hit issuer tokens.
articles.body_md:
The XRP Ledger activated the fixCleanup3_4_0 amendment on Nov. 4 at 2:52 p.m. UTC, closing a loophole that let a delegate cleared only to burn tokens create new ones in some cases, [XRPSCAN](https://xrpscan.com/amendment/fixCleanup3_4_0) and [Unchained](https://unchainedcrypto.com/xrp-ledger-turns-on-fix-for-delegated-burn-permission-that-could-mint-new-tokens/) report.

The amendment shipped with xrpld 3.4.0, the reference server release published Sept. 17. RippleX's [3.4.0 release post](https://xrpl.org/blog/2026/xrpld-3.4.0) says the bundle now "Rejects PaymentBurn payments that cross a zero balance." XRPSCAN lists enablement in the flag ledger around 108,112,128, with 33 of 35 trusted validators voting for it.

**What PaymentBurn was supposed to do**

Permission delegation lets one XRPL account hand specific powers to another. PaymentBurn is meant to let a delegate remove fungible tokens on an issuer's behalf: trust-line tokens and multi-purpose tokens (MPTs). Before the fix, documentation warned that a delegate with that permission was also able to mint new tokens in certain circumstances. Other granular permissions were not affected, and the native XRP supply was not involved, Unchained reported from the docs and the release post.

Until activation, the practical safeguard was a line in the docs asking issuers not to delegate PaymentBurn at all. With the amendment live, the ledger itself rejects the zero-crossing burn payment that created the mint path.

XRPL amendments need more than 80% of trusted validators for two straight weeks. XRPSCAN shows majority support from Oct. 21 through enablement. Unchained said an earlier run that began Oct. 9 lost the majority on Oct. 21 about 12 days in, then restarted the same day.

The change is separate from the payment-engine integer overflow that had a path to affect XRP's fixed supply. That issue was patched in xrpld 3.4.1 without an amendment vote, Unchained reported earlier. XRP traded near $1.32 at 5:57 a.m. ET Thursday, up about 2.2% over 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/xrp).

*In our opinion: the bigger story is how long the warning-label period lasted. Delegation was live on mainnet while the only guardrail was documentation telling issuers not to grant PaymentBurn. Issuers that want a separate burn account can now do it under protocol rules instead of a docs caveat. The next check is whether any issuer that delayed delegation turns it on now that the fix is live.*

articles.title: American Bitcoin Posts $126 Million Q3 Profit on Asset Gains
articles.excerpt: Mining revenue was $63.4 million. A $197.3 million gain on digital assets drove the swing from a $57.2 million Q2 loss.
articles.body_md:
American Bitcoin Corp. reported about $126 million in net income for the third quarter, swinging from a $57.2 million loss in the prior quarter, the company said in an [SEC press release furnished with its Nov. 4 Form 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1755953/000119312526447441/abtc-ex99_1.htm).

Mining revenue was about $63.4 million, down from about $67.0 million in the second quarter. The company mined about 891 bitcoin in the quarter, versus about 932 in Q2, and said its cost to mine rose to about $42,100 per bitcoin from about $36,500, citing higher seasonal power costs.

**Where the profit came from**

The income statement shows a $197.3 million gain on digital assets in Q3, against a $71.2 million digital-asset loss in Q2. A $64.3 million loss on derivatives cut the other way. Adjusted EBITDA, a non-GAAP measure defined in the release, was about $221 million, versus an Adjusted EBITDA loss of about $45.0 million in Q2.

American Bitcoin is a majority-owned subsidiary of Hut 8 and trades as ABTC. It combines self-mining with a strategic bitcoin reserve. Holdings rose from about 8,002 bitcoin on June 30 to about 8,427 on Sept. 30, including about 3,090 bitcoin pledged for miner purchases under Bitmain agreements, the release says. Satoshis per share, the company's metric of bitcoin attributable to each common share, rose about 5% over the quarter.

How fair-value accounting works here: when bitcoin's market price rises, companies that mark holdings to fair value can book paper gains through net income even if they do not sell. Those gains can reverse if prices fall. The [10-Q for the period ended Sept. 30](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1755953/000119312526447413/abtc-20260930.htm) shows the same $126.0 million net income and lists bitcoin holdings at a fair value of $257.8 million at quarter-end against a $371.7 million miner purchase liability. Gross margin on mining was about 41% in Q3, down from about 49% in Q2. The owned fleet stood at about 89,242 miners and about 28.1 EH/s of capacity at quarter-end.

Bitcoin traded near $80,240 at 5:57 a.m. ET Thursday, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion: the stake for readers is how much of the $126 million is cash mining profit versus mark-to-market. The release's own table puts the digital-asset gain at $197.3 million and the derivative loss at $64.3 million, so the swing lives mostly in accounting on the bitcoin pile. The next checkable figure is whether Satoshis per share keeps rising after power costs eased from the summer peak.*

articles.title: Bitcoin ETFs Take In $74.6 Million After Three Outflow Days
articles.excerpt: Fidelity's FBTC alone took in $236.7 million. BlackRock's IBIT still lost $201.2 million on the same session, per Farside.
articles.body_md:
U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs posted a net $74.6 million inflow on Nov. 4, the first positive day after three straight outflow sessions, [Farside Investors](https://farside.co.uk/btc/) data show.

The print is small next to what left before it. The funds shed $643.2 million on Oct. 30, $398.6 million on Nov. 2 and $115.6 million on Nov. 3. Wednesday's inflow recovers a slice of that $1.16 billion three-day exit.

**Fidelity in, BlackRock out**

The net figure hides a split. Fidelity's FBTC took in $236.7 million. BlackRock's IBIT, still the largest fund in the group, recorded a $201.2 million outflow. Bitwise's BITB added $15.2 million, ARK 21Shares' ARKB $19.9 million and Invesco's BTCO $4.0 million. Other listed funds printed zero, Farside's table shows.

Here's how the wrappers work. Authorized participants create or redeem ETF shares against bitcoin held in custody. Net creations show up as inflows; net redemptions as outflows. A day when one big fund creates while another redeems can still print a modest net gain even when the two largest products pull in opposite directions.

U.S. spot ether ETFs also flipped positive the same day, with a $53.0 million net inflow, per [Farside's ether tracker](https://farside.co.uk/eth/). BlackRock's ETHA led with $32.8 million; Bitwise's ETHB lost $22.4 million.

Bitcoin traded near $80,240 at 5:57 a.m. ET Thursday, up about 2.2% over 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin). The four-session score since Oct. 30 still sits near a $1.08 billion net outflow for the bitcoin funds.

*In our opinion: chase the split before the headline. FBTC's $236.7 million creation more than covered IBIT's $201.2 million redemption, a rotation inside the wrapper, with modest net new cash. The group is still about $1.08 billion underwater since Oct. 30. Friday's print will show whether Wednesday was a pause or a turn.*

articles.title: Trump Media Wallets Send 4,259 Bitcoin to Crypto.com
articles.excerpt: The coins match the 4,260.73 BTC pledged behind Trump Media's convertible debt, which holders can redeem for up to about $1 billion on Nov. 30.
articles.body_md:
Wallets linked to Trump Media & Technology Group sent 4,259 bitcoin, worth about $344 million, to Crypto.com at 9:17 p.m. ET Wednesday, [Lookonchain](https://lookonchain.com/feeds/80531) data show.

The coins left in two transfers of 2,140.03 BTC and 2,119.31 BTC from addresses that [Arkham Intelligence](https://arkm.com/explorer/entity/trump-media) labels as collateral for the company's convertible debt due 2028, [The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/converge/tradfi-and-fintech/trump-media-linked-wallets-send-4-259-btc-to-crypto-com) and [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/11/05/trump-media-moves-usd434-million-in-bitcoin-to-crypto-com-blockchain-data-show) reported. Both outlets put the amount at about 30% of the bitcoin Trump Media disclosed holding as of July 31.

The size lines up with the company's own books. Its [second-quarter filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849635/000143774926026777/djt20260630_10q.htm) shows 4,260.73 bitcoin serving as collateral for that debt as of June 30.

**Why the date matters**

A [Nov. 2 merger filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849635/000143774926034438/djt20261029_s4a.htm) with the SEC says holders of that debt can require Trump Media to buy it back for cash on Nov. 30. If all of them do, the bill could reach about $1.0 billion. The filing says the company may refinance with a new credit facility, raise other debt or equity, or sell its bitcoin or other digital assets to fund repurchases.

Here's how the debt works. Trump Media sold $1.0 billion of zero-interest convertible notes in May 2025 at a 4% discount, raising $960 million, per the filing. Holders can convert them into stock or, on Nov. 30, ask for full face value in cash. The pledged bitcoin backs that promise, and the quarterly filing says the company can't withdraw it unless it meets the terms of the indenture (the bond contract).

**What the data can't show**

A transfer to an exchange is not a sale. Coins on an exchange can sit in custody, back a loan or wait for a later trade, and blockchain data show only where they went. We found no public statement from Trump Media on the transfer as of 12:15 a.m. ET Thursday.

Bitcoin traded at $80,513 at 11:54 p.m. ET Wednesday, up 4.3% over 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion:* Moving almost the whole collateral pile less than four weeks before a $1 billion put date gets attention, but a transfer is not a sale. If many holders ask for cash, the bitcoin stack is a big part of what the company could tap. Watch for an 8-K on refinancing or repurchases before Nov. 30, and for any further moves out of those Crypto.com addresses.

articles.title: Philippine Inflation Jumps to 7.8% as Fuel Costs Bite
articles.excerpt: Transport prices rose 20.1% from a year earlier and drove most of October's increase, while rice was up 20.7%, keeping pressure on the central bank.
articles.body_md:
Philippine inflation rose to 7.8% in October from 7.2% in September, the Philippine Statistics Authority reported Thursday morning in Manila, the highest since February 2023, per [Philstar](https://www.philstar.com/business/2026/11/05/2568051/fuel-transport-costs-push-inflation-78-october-2026) and [GMA News](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/money/economy/1008340/inflation-rises-to-7-8-in-october/story/).

A year earlier the rate was 1.7%. The year-to-date average is 5.6%, above the government's 2% to 4% target range, [GMA News](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/money/economy/1008340/inflation-rises-to-7-8-in-october/story/) and [Rappler](https://www.rappler.com/business/inflation-rate-philippines-october-2026/) reported.

**What drove it**

Transport inflation jumped to 20.1% from 14.6% and accounted for 62.9% of the increase, GMA News reported. Housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels rose to 9.3% from 8.4%. Rice prices were up 20.7% from a year earlier, per [The Manila Times](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/11/05/business/inflation-climbs-to-78-in-october/2462382) and GMA News. Core inflation (which strips out volatile food and energy) reached 5.4%, per Philstar and Rappler. Food inflation eased from September, though outlets reported slightly different figures for that index.

Here's how an oil shock spreads. Fuel costs hit first at the pump, then in jeepney and bus fares, then in the cost of trucking rice and vegetables to market. When core inflation climbs too, the pressure has moved past energy into everyday prices. A central bank answers by raising rates, which makes borrowing dearer and slows spending.

**The policy response**

The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas raised its policy rate by 50 basis points to 5.5% on Oct. 22, its fourth straight hike, [Nikkei Asia](https://asia.nikkei.com/business/markets/philippines-raises-key-rate-to-5.5-as-inflation-saps-growth) and [GMA News](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/money/economy/1006812/bsp-hikes-rates-by-50-basis-points-amid-expected-inflation-el-ni-o-effects/story/) reported. The BSP said it expects inflation to stay high through 2027 and approach its 3% target in 2028. Its next scheduled meeting is Dec. 17, per a [UOB research note](https://uob.com.sg/assets/web-resources/research/pdf/MN_261023.pdf).

The government also plans a 3-billion-peso fuel subsidy for about 300,000 farmers, fisherfolk and drivers, the state-run [Philippine News Agency](https://www.pna.gov.ph/article/govt-to-strengthen-food-production-provide-support-to-sectors-affected-by-high-fuel-costs) reported.

*In our opinion:* A one-month swing from 14.6% to 20.1% in transport costs is the kind of number that shows up in grocery bills a few weeks later. The stake is household budgets in a country where both the central bank and the treasury are now spending ammunition on the same problem. Watch the Dec. 17 BSP decision and the November reading in early December to see whether lower global oil prices reach Manila's pumps.

articles.title: Bitcoin Climbs Back Above $80,000 as Short Sellers Get Squeezed
articles.excerpt: Bitcoin traded near $80,500 Wednesday evening, up 3.5% in a day, after an election-night dip. Short sellers took most of the forced losses.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin traded at $80,498 at 6:03 p.m. ET Wednesday, up 3.5% in 24 hours per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin). That erased an election-night slide. Ether did better, rising 6.1% to $2,429.

The round trip took about 12 hours. On Coinbase, bitcoin bottomed near $75,600 in the 10 p.m. ET hour Tuesday as midterm results came in, then touched $81,130 in the 10 a.m. hour Wednesday, [Unchained](https://unchainedcrypto.com/bitcoin-tops-81000-after-midterm-dip-squeezing-short-sellers/) reported.

**Shorts paid for the bounce**

About $950 million of leveraged crypto positions were wiped out over 24 hours, Unchained reported, citing CoinGlass data. Shorts made up about $560 million of that, or roughly 59%. Traders who bet on an election hangover got one. It just wasn't the kind they ordered.

Here is how that works. A short seller borrows to bet that a price will fall. If the price rises far enough instead, the exchange closes the bet to cover the loan, which means buying the coin back at market. Those forced purchases push the price higher, which can trip the next batch of shorts. Traders call that chain a short squeeze.

Sentiment hasn't caught up with the chart. The [Crypto Fear & Greed Index](https://alternative.me/crypto/fear-and-greed-index/) read 34 on Wednesday, still in fear territory.

The policy picture is also shifting. Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate, [Reuters](https://cyprus-mail.com/2026/11/04/oil-slumps-after-midterm-election-raises-bets-on-iran-war-exit) reported, so the committees that write crypto market rules change hands in January. Whether that speeds up or slows down a market-structure bill is an open question, and lawmakers in both parties have backed parts of past bills.

*In our opinion:* A 6% swing in half a day says more about leverage than about ballots. Plenty of traders leaned short into the results and were forced to buy back higher. Watch Thursday's spot ETF flows: a bounce driven by forced buying needs real buyers behind it to last.

articles.title: Block Books $764 Million for a Planned DOJ Bank Secrecy Act Deal
articles.excerpt: Cash App owner Block set aside $764 million for a planned three-year deferred prosecution deal with the DOJ over its anti-money laundering program.
articles.body_md:
Block, the company behind Cash App and Square, has accrued $764 million for a planned deal with the U.S. Justice Department, its [quarterly report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1512673/000162828026069524/xyz-20260930.htm) filed Tuesday shows. The deal is not final.

Block and the DOJ reached an agreement in principle in October, the filing says. Under it, prosecutors would defer for three years "a charge that the Company failed to maintain an effective anti-money laundering program in violation of the Bank Secrecy Act." If Block meets every obligation for those three years, the DOJ would move to dismiss the charge with prejudice, which means it could not be brought again.

**How a deferred prosecution works**

A deferred prosecution agreement is a middle path between a trial and walking away. Prosecutors file a charge but park it. The company pays money and accepts conditions, which can include outside monitors. Break the terms, and the charge can come back. Block's filing warns that failing to meet the terms "could subject us to prosecution on the deferred charge, or additional penalties."

The planned payment has a gross figure of about $964 million. Block expects to pay about $764 million net, after credit for earlier regulatory settlements. One of those came in January 2025, when Block settled with a group of state money-transmission regulators over parts of its anti-money laundering program, the filing says. [Unchained](https://unchainedcrypto.com/block-books-764-million-for-planned-doj-deal-that-would-defer-a-bank-secrecy-act-charge/) reported that the accrual was $526 million at the end of June.

Block's side is in the filing too. The company says the deal still needs "a final agreement satisfactory to all parties and court approval," and that it cannot promise one will be reached. The inquiries began shortly after a short seller's report in March 2023. SEC staff told Block in March 2026 that they had closed their own investigation without recommending enforcement action.

*In our opinion:* Nearly a billion dollars gross is the price tag for a compliance gap, and the bill has grown since June. The bigger stake is the next three years, when a deferred charge hangs over the company. Watch for the final agreement and any monitor terms, because those decide how Cash App checks its customers.

Cash App lets everyday users buy and sell bitcoin, so its compliance rules shape one of the main retail routes into crypto in the U.S.

articles.title: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa Confirms Attack Behind a $133M Crypto Money Trail
articles.excerpt: French bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa says attackers used its own account for fraudulent transfers and backs the rough size of a $133 million crypto trail.
articles.body_md:
French cooperative bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa said Wednesday that outside attackers used one of its own accounts to make fraudulent transfers. On-chain investigator ZachXBT had traced more than $133 million moving through crypto exchanges.

In a [statement](https://www.cm-arkea.com/arkea/banque/assurances/pa_38386/fr/informations-complementaires-suite-a-l-attaque-dont-le-credit-mutuel-arkea-a-ete-victime) posted at 5:30 p.m. Paris time, or 11:30 a.m. ET, the bank said the attackers came in through "the platform of one of our service providers" and reached the bank directly (our translation). It denied press reports that they entered through Fortuneo, its online bank. Client accounts were not used, and client holdings are unaffected, the bank said.

**The bank backs the size, not the number**

Asked whether €118 million, or $133 million, had been stolen, the bank said it does not confirm those figures and "can simply validate the order of magnitude." Part of the money may have been blocked, and recovery efforts are under way, it said. It added that the amounts do not threaten its financial health.

The path from bank to blockchain matters here. According to the bank, the attackers sent money from its account to other banks. From there, it says, the cash may have been converted into crypto on specialist platforms. That turns ordinary bank transfers into stablecoins, which can leave an exchange for a private wallet within minutes.

Blockchain data firm Bitquery traced $108.8 million in USDC withdrawn from Kraken, Crypto.com and OKX in about 21 hours, [Cyberattaque.org](https://www.cyberattaque.org/credit-mutuel-arkea-lombre-dun-detournement-de-133-millions-de-dollars-en-cryptomonnaies/) reported. Bitquery found about $63 million of stablecoins swapped into 27,553 ETH within four hours, the site reported. Kraken and Crypto.com said they restricted linked accounts and that their own systems were not breached, it added.

No one has been named or charged. The bank says it is working with police and judicial authorities.

*In our opinion:* This is a bank hack first and a crypto story second, but the speed of the exit is the crypto part. Stablecoins made the money portable within hours, and exchange freezes are the main brake. Watch how much Arkéa recovers and whether its service provider is named.

articles.title: Schroders Puts an Emerging-Market Bond Fund on Solana
articles.excerpt: Schroders, which manages more than $1 trillion, is offering its emerging-market bond strategy on Solana through Centrifuge, its first deployment on that chain.
articles.body_md:
Schroders, the London asset manager with more than $1 trillion under management, launched a tokenized emerging-market bond fund on Solana on Wednesday through Centrifuge, a [Centrifuge post](https://centrifuge.io/blog/schroders-centrifuge) said. It is the firm's first deployment on that network.

This one is not a cash fund. Most tokenized funds so far hold Treasuries or money market assets. This one holds bonds from governments and companies in developing economies. "Emerging markets debt introduces a fundamentally different source of risk and return," Centrifuge's Anil Sood said, as [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/business/2026/11/04/global-asset-manager-schroders-brings-emerging-market-bond-fund-to-solana) reported.

**How the token works**

Buyers do not hold the Schroders fund directly. They get SISF tokens in a British Virgin Islands feeder fund, which in turn owns shares of Schroder International Selection Fund Emerging Market Bond, a Luxembourg fund, according to Centrifuge's [fund page](https://app.centrifuge.io/pool/281474976710677). Token values track that fund's net asset value. Subscriptions and redemptions are made in stablecoins, and redemptions settle three business days later.

The doors are narrow. The fund is open only to non-U.S. professional investors, with a minimum of 100,000 USDC. The page lists underlying fund fees of 1.29% and says the feeder has no operating history of its own.

Schroders has managed emerging-market debt for more than 50 years. Marita Mcginley, its head of operations for Asia-Pacific and digital assets, said tokenizing the strategy lets the firm reach "a new generation of investors." Solana carries more than $4 billion in tokenized real-world assets, Centrifuge said.

*In our opinion:* Moving riskier credit onto a public chain is a bigger step than parking cash there, and it tests whether onchain buyers want yield with real default and currency risk. The early size is small. Watch whether SISF tokens get accepted as collateral in Solana lending apps, because that is where tokenization stops being a wrapper and starts being plumbing.

articles.title: Oil Falls More Than 8% as Traders Bet on an Exit From the Iran War
articles.excerpt: Brent settled at $94.62 and WTI at $88.12 Wednesday, both down more than 8%, as traders bet the midterm results could speed an end to the Iran war.
articles.body_md:
Brent crude settled at $94.62 a barrel Wednesday, down 8.7%, and U.S. West Texas Intermediate fell 8.3% to $88.12, [Reuters](https://cyprus-mail.com/2026/11/04/oil-slumps-after-midterm-election-raises-bets-on-iran-war-exit) reported. Both closed at their lowest since Aug. 31.

Oil futures have fallen more than 14% this week, [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/04/oil-price-iran-war-us-election-strait-hormuz.html) reported, after gaining more than 10% in October on fears of a bigger conflict.

**Why traders sold**

Democrats won control of the House and the Senate in Tuesday's midterms. Traders bet the new balance could hasten an end to the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran, which has disrupted energy supplies for eight months. President Donald Trump told the Financial Times on Tuesday that the U.S. had no immediate plans to strike Iran. He also said gasoline prices hurt his party with voters. Vice President JD Vance said on social media that the war was the reason Republicans lost.

Not everyone reads it that way. "I'm more concerned that we can see an escalation in Iran sooner than a resolution," said Carl Larry of Enverus, per Reuters. Rapidan Energy's Bob McNally told CNBC the odds still favor military escalation. Iran's supreme leader said U.S. hostility would continue whichever party holds power.

Here is how a war moves oil. Prices carry a risk premium, an extra amount traders pay for the chance that supply gets cut. Gulf exports averaged 17.1 million barrels a day in October, roughly three-quarters of pre-war levels, Reuters reported, citing Vortexa. When a deal looks likelier, that premium shrinks fast.

Pump prices lag. The national gasoline average was $4.12 Wednesday morning, [NBC News](https://finance.yahoo.com/energy/articles/oil-prices-drop-below-100-170501842.html) reported.

*In our opinion:* An 8% drop in a day prices in a lot of peace that hasn't been signed yet. Analysts on both sides have a point, and the gap between them is where the next swing comes from. Watch diesel and gasoline over the next few weeks, because that is where any relief would show up for households.

For crypto, cheaper oil can cool inflation, which shapes the path for interest rates that also moves bitcoin.

articles.title: Circle Cuts About 5% of Staff as ARC Presale Lifts Revenue to $865M
articles.excerpt: Circle's revenue rose 17% to $865 million, helped by a $182 million token presale, while lower rates cut reserve income and the company trimmed about 5% of staff.
articles.body_md:
Circle Internet Group cut about 5% of its workforce in the third quarter, even as revenue and reserve income rose 17% to $865 million. A one-time token sale did much of the lifting.

The staff cut cost about $9.15 million in restructuring charges, mostly severance and related pay, [Bitcoin.com News reported](https://news.bitcoin.com/stablecoins/circle-q3-revenue-865m-usdc-issuer-cuts-workforce/) from Circle's filing. Decrypt also reported the 5% reduction. Circle tied the move to aligning staff with its operating model and priorities.

**A $182 million token sale did the heavy lifting**

Other revenue jumped to $207 million, and $182 million of it came from the presale of ARC, the token for Circle's new Arc blockchain, the company's [results release](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261104960710/en/Circle-Reports-Third-Quarter-2026-Results) shows. Net income from continuing operations rose 5% to $226 million. Adjusted EBITDA climbed 85% to $317 million.

Here is how the core business works: every USDC is backed by cash and short-term U.S. government debt. Circle earns the interest on those reserves, then pays a large share to partners, such as exchanges, that hand USDC to users. When interest rates fall, that income shrinks even if more coins are in circulation.

That happened this quarter. Reserve income fell 8% to $658 million as Circle's return on reserves dropped 0.61 percentage point to 3.5%. Average USDC in circulation rose 8% from a year earlier to $73.3 billion, and supply ended the quarter at $73.9 billion. Distribution and transaction costs fell 8% to $412 million.

**Usage grew faster than supply**

Onchain USDC transaction volume rose 49% to $13.9 trillion. Still, USDC's share of the dollar-backed stablecoin market slipped 1.83 percentage points to 27%, the release says. Circle kept its full-year guidance unchanged, executives said on the [earnings call](https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-circle-tops-q3-2026-eps-estimates-on-strong-growth-93CH-5000408).

*In our opinion:* Take out the $182 million presale and other revenue drops to roughly $25 million, so a big piece of this quarter's growth came from a sale Circle has not shown it can repeat. The core business still rises and falls with interest rates and with how many dollars sit in USDC. Next quarter's reserve income and market share will show whether the slide in both has stopped.

articles.title: Riot Leases Its Whole Corsicana Campus to an AI Lab for $28 Billion
articles.excerpt: Bitcoin miner Riot signed a 15-year lease for 910 megawatts in Texas with an unnamed AI lab, worth about $28 billion, and says it won't need to sell new shares.
articles.body_md:
Riot Platforms signed a 15-year lease for its entire Corsicana, Texas, campus with an unnamed AI lab, a deal the bitcoin miner values at about $28 billion over the initial term. It announced the lease Wednesday in its third-quarter report.

The tenant is the same lab that signed a lease at Riot's Rockdale site earlier this year, the company said. Rent averages about $1.8 billion a year, including built-in annual increases. Two five-year extensions would lift the total to about $54 billion. CEO Jason Les called it "the largest lease in Riot's history."

**Riot brings the land and power, the lab brings the chips**

The deal is a "triple-net powered land lease." In plain words, Riot delivers 332 acres, the grid connection and powered pads, which are prepared sites wired for electricity. The tenant buys, installs and runs its own computers and pays nearly all operating costs, power included. Rent is owed on the full 910 megawatts whether the lab uses it or not.

That setup keeps Riot's bill low. Building costs about $6 million per megawatt, or $5.5 billion in all, roughly half a typical data center build, Riot says. Riot pays $2 million per megawatt itself. The other $4 million is reimbursed to the tenant after each phase starts paying rent, funded with project debt or, failing that, rent credits. Riot says it does not expect to issue new shares. [Blockspace](https://blockspace.media/insight/riot-signs-corsicana-ai-lease/) also reported the lease terms.

Power arrives in three steps: 400 megawatts in September 2027, 200 in January 2028 and 310 in July 2028.

**Mining still pays most of the bills**

Bitcoin mining brought in $116.0 million of Riot's $181.4 million in quarterly revenue, down from $160.8 million a year earlier as its average bitcoin price fell to $70,855. Riot mined 1,637 bitcoin in the quarter. It has sold 20,264 bitcoin this year for about $1.5 billion, mostly to fund data centers, and held 2,418 at Sept. 30.

*In our opinion:* Riot now has $38 billion of signed lease revenue and one lab behind most of it, which makes this a miner turning landlord with a very large tenant. That is a sturdier income stream than block rewards, as long as the tenant keeps paying. The date to circle is September 2027, when the first 400 megawatts are due and rent starts within 60 days.

articles.title: Morgan Stanley Tokenizes U.S. Stocks and Treasuries Through DTCC
articles.excerpt: Morgan Stanley says it is among the first banks to turn U.S. stocks and Treasuries into tokens through DTCC's new service, which went live Oct. 28.
articles.body_md:
Morgan Stanley said it has turned U.S. stocks and Treasuries into blockchain tokens through the Depository Trust & Clearing Corp.'s new tokenization service, putting it among the first of 20 signed-up firms to use the system, [Decrypt](https://decrypt.co/382513/wall-streets-plumbing-onchain-morgan-stanley-tokenizes-securities) reported. [Crypto Times](https://www.cryptotimes.io/2026/11/04/morgan-stanley-among-first-to-use-dtccs-tokenization-service/) also reported the bank's statement, which it made in a post on X.

The service went live Oct. 28, DTCC said in its [launch release](https://www.dtcc.com/press-releases/2026/dtcc-tokenization-service-goes-live). Its Depository Trust Co. unit holds more than $114 trillion in assets. Twenty firms signed up at launch, including Morgan Stanley, Bank of America, Citi, J.P. Morgan, Citadel Securities and UBS.

**How a "digital twin" works**

DTC already holds the securities on behalf of banks and brokers. Under the new service, an eligible firm asks DTC to mint a token that stands for a security it holds there. DTCC calls the token a digital twin. It keeps the ownership rights, investor protections and economic entitlements of the original, and it can be converted back.

The timing is where it gets interesting. Conversion orders are taken on weekdays from 2 a.m. to 6 p.m. ET. Once minted, tokens can move between approved wallets 24 hours a day, seven days a week, a [DTC notice](https://files.dtcc.com/download/assets/DAS-001/8a31d732d2d311f1a30ef632b7f70f6d) says.

The first assets allowed are Russell 1000 stocks, major index ETFs and U.S. Treasuries, under a December 2025 no-action letter from SEC staff, according to DTCC. The tokens run on the Canton Network and on a private network DTCC operates.

**What we don't know yet**

Neither DTCC nor Morgan Stanley has said how much value has been tokenized so far. Fees for the service were not in the launch release.

*In our opinion:* Twenty firms have signed up, but the number to watch is how much actually gets minted. The weekend transfers are the most crypto-like part: a token can change hands on a Saturday while the stock market is closed, with the country's main custodian still behind it. If big banks start using that, tokenization stops being a pilot and starts being plumbing.

articles.title: Euro Zone Inflation Hits 4%, Highest Since 2023, as Energy Jumps
articles.excerpt: Energy prices rose 20.8% from a year earlier, but core inflation held at 2.5%. Markets put the odds of a December ECB hike above 72%.
articles.body_md:
Prices in the euro zone rose 4.0% in the year to October, Eurostat's flash estimate showed Wednesday, up from 3.8% in September. It's the first reading at 4% or higher since September 2023, when inflation hit 4.3%, CNBC reported.

Energy did most of the work.

Energy prices were 20.8% higher than a year earlier, up from 18.9% in September, while inflation excluding energy held at 2.3%. Services rose 3.3%.

**Core inflation didn't budge**

Core inflation, which strips out energy, food, alcohol and tobacco, stayed at 2.5%, Eurostat's table shows. The European Central Bank aims for 2%. All 21 euro countries are above that, from 2.3% in Malta to 6.1% in Lithuania, CNBC reported.

How the number gets made: a flash estimate is Eurostat's first quick read, published at the end of the month before every price is in. The full October figures, which can revise it, are due Nov. 18.

**December hike odds near 72%**

The ECB held its key rate at 2.5% in October after a 0.25-percentage-point hike in September. After Wednesday's release, markets priced more than a 72% chance of another hike at the bank's December meeting, CNBC reported. The 4.0% matched the forecast of economists polled by Reuters.

Why crypto readers care: higher rates raise what savers earn on cash and bonds. That lifts the bar for assets that pay no interest, like bitcoin. The euro rose 0.6% against the dollar Wednesday morning, per CNBC, and bitcoin was near $78,490 at 5:55 a.m. ET, up 2.0% in 24 hours, per CoinGecko.

*In our opinion: watch core at 2.5% before the 4% headline. With energy doing nearly all the lifting, the ECB has to decide whether to raise rates against a price shock that its rate tools don't produce. Nov. 18 brings the full data, and the December meeting brings the answer.*

articles.title: Hong Kong Passes Crypto Tax Reporting Law, Data Collection Starts 2027
articles.excerpt: Crypto exchanges and brokers tied to Hong Kong must register with the tax office and collect customer data. Sharing with other countries starts in 2028.
articles.body_md:
Hong Kong lawmakers passed a bill Wednesday that makes crypto service providers collect customer tax data starting Jan. 1, 2027, the government said. The city's tax office will begin sharing that data with partner jurisdictions in 2028.

The law brings in the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework, or CARF, a standard the OECD published in 2023. The OECD is the Paris-based group of mostly advanced economies that also wrote the global rules for swapping bank account data. CARF creates no new tax. It lets tax offices see crypto activity that existing tax rules already cover.

**How the reporting works**

Exchanges, brokers and similar firms with a qualifying link to Hong Kong must run due-diligence checks on customers, collect the required transaction information and report it to the Inland Revenue Department once a year. The department then exchanges it automatically with partner tax authorities, on a reciprocal basis, the government said.

Every covered provider must register on the department's CARF portal, even with nothing to report. Registration is due by Jan. 31 of the year after a firm first meets the law's tests, the IRD's guidance page says.

A second part updates the Common Reporting Standard, which Hong Kong has used since 2018 to swap financial account data. The amended version adds digital financial products. It takes effect in 2028, with the first exchanges under it in 2029.

**Providers carry the cost**

The paperwork falls on the platforms, which must build the checks and reports. The IRD said it will issue guidance and has set up a dedicated team to field industry questions. The government's release doesn't estimate how many firms are covered or what compliance will cost.

Christopher Hui, the secretary for financial services and the treasury, said matching the latest standards "will reinforce the confidence" of crypto service providers, financial institutions and digital asset users. The bill was gazetted May 22 and had its first reading on June 3, according to the IRD.

*In our opinion: the bill's official title runs 13 words, and the part that matters fits in one date. From Jan. 1, 2027, Hong Kong platforms start building files on customers, and those files start crossing borders in 2028. The document worth chasing next is the IRD's guidance, because that's where providers learn exactly how much work they've signed up for.*

articles.title: Bitcoin Dips to $75,740 on Election Night, Recovers Above $77,000
articles.excerpt: Stock futures fell and Treasury yields dropped as midterm results came in. Bitcoin's slide lasted about two hours before it climbed back into the green.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin fell to about $75,740 at 10:10 p.m. ET on Tuesday, CoinGecko data shows, as U.S. stock futures dropped on early midterm election results. By 11:55 p.m. it was back near $77,300, up 0.5% over 24 hours.

That round trip took under two hours. It happened while Wall Street was repricing the chance that control of Congress changes hands in January, which matters for crypto because every federal crypto bill has to clear both the House and the Senate.

**Futures fell, bonds rallied**

Contracts tied to the S&P 500 lost 1.1% and Nasdaq-100 futures slid 2% as results rolled in, [CNBC reported](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/03/treasury-yields-fall-as-democrats-win-big-in-us-midterm-elections.html) at 10:24 p.m. ET. A CNBC Election Desk projection had Democrats winning the House, while the Senate was still undecided at that hour.

Bonds moved the other way. The 10-year Treasury yield dropped nearly 5 basis points to 4.902%, and the 2-year fell 6 basis points to 4.55%. (A basis point is 0.01 percentage point.) When investors buy bonds for safety, bond prices rise and yields fall, because a bond's fixed payments are now worth more relative to its price.

**Fund flows were already negative**

U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs had net outflows of $115.6 million on Tuesday and ether ETFs lost $85.3 million, [Farside Investors](https://farside.co.uk/btc/) data shows. Those figures cover the regular trading day, before polls closed.

What isn't known yet: the final makeup of the Senate. Projections can change as counting continues, and CNBC's House call was a projection, not a certified result. Before the vote, JPMorgan told clients a Democratic sweep could knock the S&P 500 down about 0.5% on Wednesday, [CNBC reported](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/03/midterm-election-stock-market.html).

*In our opinion: the move that counts comes after the counting stops. A $1,500 dip that reversed within two hours is small next to a 2% drop in Nasdaq futures. The next thing to check is the Senate call, because both chambers have to agree before any crypto market-structure bill reaches the president.*

articles.title: Block Lifts 2026 Outlook as Its Bitcoin Gross Profit Halves
articles.excerpt: Cash App sold $1.80 billion of bitcoin last quarter but kept $52 million of it as gross profit after a fee cut. Block now sees 2026 gross profit of $12.63 billion.
articles.body_md:
Block raised its 2026 gross profit forecast to $12.626 billion on Tuesday after a third quarter in which its bitcoin business earned half as much gross profit as a year earlier, its [shareholder letter](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1512673/000162828026069513/q32026shareholderletter.htm) shows.

The old forecast was $12.51 billion, [Reuters reported](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/block-raises-fullyear-profit-outlook-as-cash-app-drives-q3-growth-4996401). Block's shares rose 6% to 8% in after-hours trading, according to [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/block-surges-8-on-earnings-beat-and-raised-guidance-4996458) and [The Block](https://www.theblock.co/news/business/2026-11-03-block-q3-earnings-shares-rise-432585).

**Big revenue, thin margin**

Bitcoin ecosystem revenue was $1.80 billion in the quarter, down from $2.02 billion. Gross profit on it fell 50% to $52 million.

Why the gap is so wide: when a Cash App customer buys bitcoin, Block books the full purchase price as revenue, then books the cost of buying that bitcoin as a cost. Only the difference, mostly fees and spread, is gross profit. Block said the drop came mainly from "a strategic decision to reduce the fee we charge on certain bitcoin transactions on Cash App."

The rest of the company carried the quarter. Total gross profit rose 22% to $3.24 billion, Cash App's rose 27% and Square's rose 14%. Adjusted earnings were $1.13 a share, against 54 cents a year earlier.

**The bitcoin on Block's own books**

Block also holds bitcoin as an investment. It recorded a $229.7 million remeasurement gain on that holding in the quarter and valued it at $771.9 million on Sept. 30, the filing shows.

Costs rose too. Losses on transactions, loans and consumer receivables climbed 66% to $601.7 million as Cash App lending grew, Reuters reported.

*In our opinion: the number worth watching is $52 million. Block chose to earn less per bitcoin trade while the rest of the business grew, which tells you bitcoin is being priced to bring customers in. If the fee cut lifts trading volume, revenue should show it first. Fourth-quarter results land Feb. 24, 2027.*

articles.title: South Korea's Ruling Party Seeks a Fourth Delay of Its Crypto Tax
articles.excerpt: The tax would take 22% of yearly crypto gains above 2.5 million won starting Jan. 1. Lawmakers mostly discussed pushing it back about two years.
articles.body_md:
South Korea's ruling Democratic Party formally asked the government on Wednesday to postpone a crypto income tax due to start Jan. 1, [Yonhap reported](https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20261104004600315). If accepted, it would be the fourth delay since the tax was introduced in 2020.

The tax would take 22%, including local income tax, of a person's yearly crypto gains above 2.5 million won (about $1,880), Yonhap said.

**"Time for companies and investors to adapt"**

Party leader Kim Min-seok announced the request at a supreme council meeting in Seoul. The party wants to pass the Digital Asset Basic Act first, he said, and "allow time for companies and investors to adapt." Kim also said the length of the delay would be set clearly this time, along with groundwork such as using overseas transaction data, the [Asia Business Daily reported](https://www.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2026110410165510262).

The request doesn't name a length. A day earlier, Democratic lawmaker Oh Ki-hyung said most of the party's members on the National Assembly's finance committee favored a delay, and that about two years came up most often, [according to Yonhap](https://www.yna.co.kr/view/AKR20261103052451001).

**Why overseas data drives the timing**

Yonhap said one factor is 2029, when overseas tax-data swaps get going in earnest. That refers to the OECD's Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework, or CARF, under which tax agencies automatically share users' exchange records across borders. Until it is running, Korea's tax office can see trades on domestic exchanges but has limited visibility into accounts abroad.

A bill from Democratic lawmaker Park Min-gyu would tie the start date to that system: the tax would begin on the second Jan. 1 after Korea's first CARF data exchange, which points to 2029, [The Herald Business reported](https://biz.heraldcorp.com/article/10904004).

Opposition People Power Party lawmakers, including Song Eon-seog, have filed their own bills to delay or scrap the tax, the Herald said. Reports so far don't include a government response to Wednesday's request.

*In our opinion: a fourth delay in six years would start to look like a schedule of its own. The detail to chase is the length, because a date tied to CARF would tell Korean traders when the 22% rate actually arrives. Rival bills from both parties lean toward a delay, so the length is where the real debate sits.*

articles.title: SEC Staff Call Canton Coin a 'Digital Commodity' in No-Action Letter
articles.excerpt: SEC staff say Canton Coin is a digital commodity and won't push enforcement over how it's minted, as long as the facts Digital Asset gave them hold.
articles.body_md:
Canton Coin, a token with a market value near $3.9 billion, now has a signed letter from SEC staff calling it a "digital commodity."

The SEC's Division of Corporation Finance said Tuesday in a [no-action letter](https://www.sec.gov/rules-regulations/no-action-interpretive-exemptive-letters/division-corporation-finance-no-action/canton-coin-110326) that, relying on what it was told, Canton Coin fits the "digital commodity" label in the Commission's March 2026 crypto interpretation. The staff also said it won't recommend enforcement if the coin keeps being minted as described without registering under the Securities Act or Exchange Act.

The letter, signed by Deputy Chief Counsel Jonathan Ingram, answers an [Oct. 30 request](https://www.sec.gov/files/corpfin/no-action/canton-incoming-103026.pdf) filed on behalf of Digital Asset Holdings, the company that created the Canton protocol.

**What the staff leaned on**

Two points. The staff said the coin derives its value "from the programmatic operation of the Canton Network, as well as supply and demand dynamics, rather than from the expectation of profits from the essential managerial efforts of others." And it said the network has no "central party."

**How Canton Coin works**

Per the request letter, the coin pays fees on Canton's shared transaction layer, the Global Synchronizer. Fees are set in U.S. dollars and the coin used to pay them is burned, so heavy use shrinks supply. New coins appear only as rewards to network operators and apps based on activity. The letter says there was no pre-launch sale or allocation.

Control is the other test. As of Sept. 30, the letter counts about 60 Super Validators, but only 13 node operators vote, one vote each, with two-thirds needed for changes. Digital Asset runs two of those 13 nodes.

**The fine print**

The staff wrote that "any different facts or conditions might require the Division to reach different conclusions," and that the response "does not express any legal conclusion on the issues presented." It is a staff view. Neither the Commission nor a court has ruled.

The coin was up about 3% over 24 hours at 5:55 p.m. ET, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/canton-network). It came a day after the division [updated its FAQs](https://www.sec.gov/featured-topics/crypto-task-force/cryptosec) on that interpretation.

*In our opinion:* A no-action letter is a permission slip where the fine print is basically the whole slip, and Canton's holds only while 13 node operators keep splitting the votes. It matters beyond one token, because it shows which facts the staff weighs: no presale, burned fees and no single hand on the wheel. Watch for copycat requests, and for whether Digital Asset's two-node share ever grows.

articles.title: Cboe, Citadel-Backed Group Sues CFTC to Stop Single-Stock Perps
articles.excerpt: Hours after the CFTC let perpetual futures on U.S. stocks start trading, a group backed by Cboe and Citadel Securities asked a court to undo it.
articles.body_md:
The CFTC opened the door to perpetual futures on single U.S. stocks on Tuesday. Within hours, a group backed by Cboe and Citadel Securities was in court trying to shut it.

The Capital Markets Alliance [filed suit](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261102755217/en/Capital-Markets-Alliance-Files-Suit-Challenging-CFTC-Approval-of-Single-Stock-Perpetual-Derivatives) in federal court in Manhattan asking a judge to vacate the CFTC's approval of these contracts, declare them security-based swaps, and bar the approvals from taking effect while the case runs. Its members include Cboe, Citadel Securities and the Healthy Markets Association, per a [Cboe statement](https://ir.cboe.com/news/news-details/2026/Cboe-Joins-Capital-Markets-Alliance-Challenge-to-CFTC-Approval-of-Single-Stock-Perpetual-Derivatives/default.aspx). [The Defiant reported](https://thedefiant.io/news/regulation/cboe-backed-group-sues-cftc-over-single-stock-perps-approvals) that the complaint targets approvals for Coinbase, Kalshi and Bitnomial.

**How a perp works, and why the label matters**

A perpetual future has no end date. Traders on one side pay the other a small funding fee to keep its price near the stock. The fight is over what to call it. The CFTC treats these as security futures, which fall under both the CFTC and the SEC. The alliance says they are security-based swaps, which Congress put under the SEC alone. The label decides which venues can list them and which protections apply.

**The case against**

The group argues the CFTC gave no explanation, ignored that it "has long treated perpetual derivatives as swaps," and did not weigh the impact on investors. "The hasty roll out of financial products that circumvent well-established regulatory frameworks erodes investor protection," said Adam Ford, the alliance's secretary. Cboe CEO Craig Donohue said the products "belong on registered securities platforms."

**The other side**

A CFTC spokesperson called the suit "troubling" interference, [Reuters reported](https://www.streetinsider.com/Reuters/Cboe%2C+Citadel-backed+group+sues+US+regulator+over+single-stock+perps/27279286.html): "Our markets should be governed by law, not litigation campaigns intended to block innovation." CFTC Chairman Michael Selig [said Tuesday](https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/SpeechesTestimony/seligstatement110326) the contracts sit under both agencies' rules and that exchanges must also register with the SEC to list them. The SEC did not immediately respond to Reuters. We found no public response from Coinbase, Kalshi or Bitnomial, which are not defendants.

**Follow the money**

Reuters noted that prediction-market firms see perps as a growth path on ground held by traditional firms. The Chicago Mercantile Exchange sued the CFTC in June over crypto perps from Kalshi and Coinbase.

*In our opinion:* This is a turf war about where stock bets get made, and both sides wrap their case in investor protection. The answer decides who earns fees on a product crypto traders already love. Watch whether the court grants the emergency stay, because that decides if any stock perp trades before a ruling.

articles.title: Binance Says a Fake Job Interview Opened the Door to Its $6.34B Drain
articles.excerpt: Binance's first security report traces the Oct. 29 wallet drain to a tampered install in June and a rigged coding test in September.
articles.body_md:
A rigged job interview sits at the center of how attackers took about $6.34 billion from Binance on Oct. 29, according to the exchange's [initial security report](https://www.binance.com/en/blog/community/3229153443759566763) published Tuesday.

The attackers "spent months building their way in," co-CEO Richard Teng [told CNBC's "Squawk on the Street"](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/03/binance-co-ceo-teng-says-hackers-used-fake-job-interviews-to-steal-6point3-billion-in-crypto.html) on Tuesday.

**The four-month path**

Binance said the first step came in June, when a wallet engineer downloaded a tampered Homebrew installation while searching for an AI coding tool. Binance said it spotted odd activity, replaced the device and rotated credentials, but the team's roles had already been exposed. In September, a second engineer was approached through a job platform. After a video interview, a coding "assignment" carried malware built to slip past security tools, per the report and [Unchained's summary](https://unchainedcrypto.com/binance-details-four-month-path-from-tainted-developer-install-to-6-34-billion-drain/).

On Oct. 20, the attackers used an internal AI tool to reach a container deployment token. On Oct. 29, they deployed a container, ran a script and moved funds from five hot wallets.

How does one token drain five wallets? A hot wallet is an online wallet an exchange uses for daily withdrawals. Binance said the attackers abused an Ethereum feature called EIP-7702, which lets an account hand signing power to code. Because Binance's wallets split keys across several parties (a setup called MPC), no single key could cancel that power quickly. The last transfer, 2,961.9 ETH, settled at 6:56 p.m. ET, and the access was cut at 7:10 p.m. ET, per Unchained.

**The money**

Teng told CNBC that 98% of the $6.34 billion has been replenished and that Binance is still buying harder-to-find assets. Binance's own earlier updates gave 90% on Oct. 31 and about 95% on Nov. 2, Unchained noted. Tether, Circle and Ripple have reportedly frozen about $3 billion, per CNBC.

Teng did not name North Korea, but acknowledged that the FBI has tied the attack to the TraderTraitor group. North Korea has denied the FBI's finding. Binance said it has rebuilt the affected systems and plans an independent review and a security research fund.

*In our opinion:* The scariest line here is the job interview, because any crypto engineer anywhere can get that email tomorrow. Binance's money story is getting better, but the 98% figure needs one clean, dated number everyone can check. Watch the independent review and whether withdrawals fully reopen.

articles.title: CFTC Clears Perpetual Futures on Individual Stocks for U.S. Trading
articles.excerpt: The crypto-born contract that never expires can now trade on single U.S. stocks at dual-registered exchanges, CFTC Chairman Selig said Tuesday.
articles.body_md:
Perpetual futures, the never-expiring contract that grew up on offshore crypto exchanges, can now trade on individual U.S. stocks, CFTC Chairman Michael Selig said in a [statement Tuesday](https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/SpeechesTestimony/seligstatement110326).

"Today, perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities (the 'Equity Perps') can begin trading for the first time on CFTC-registered exchanges," Selig wrote.

**Who can list them**

Per the [CFTC release](https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/9319-26), the contracts can trade only on designated contract markets that are also registered with the SEC to handle security futures. Selig said the contracts were deemed approved under CFTC Regulation 40.3 as security futures products. That puts them under both the CFTC's and the SEC's rules.

The statement did not name a specific exchange or give a launch date.

**How a perpetual works**

A normal futures contract has an end date. A perpetual does not. To keep its price close to the real asset, traders on one side pay the other a small "funding" fee every few hours. When the perp trades above the stock, buyers pay sellers, and the reverse when it trades below. That lets traders hold a bet on a stock, with leverage, for as long as they keep paying.

**Why now**

The move extends a path the agency started this year. Selig's statement points to the CFTC's May 29 approval of a bitcoin perpetual contract from KalshiEX, and to a March memorandum of understanding between the CFTC and the SEC. He said the goal is to give traders these products under U.S. protections "rather than being forced to turn to offshore, and often unregulated, venues."

Selig also cited SEC Chairman Paul Atkins, who has described such products as stuck in a regulatory "no man's land."

*In our opinion:* Crypto just exported its most popular trading tool to Wall Street, and that is a big deal for exchanges that hold both licenses. Perps bring easy leverage, so the margin rules each exchange sets will show how well investors are protected. Watch for the first exchange to list one and which stocks it picks.
